bill.title: FIND Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly protects firearm manufacturers, dealers, and trade associations from discrimination in federal contracting.
Banks and financial institutions that provide services to federal contractors would be affected if they maintain policies restricting business with firearm entities.
Defense contractors frequently hold federal contracts and may need to review policies regarding firearm-related business relationships.
Insurance companies that contract with the federal government would need to ensure their underwriting policies do not discriminate against firearm businesses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit federal agencies from awarding contracts to companies that discriminate against firearm manufacturers, dealers, or trade associations. Contractors would be required to certify they have no policies that discriminate against firearm-related businesses and will not adopt such policies during the contract term. The requirement would apply to both prime contractors and subcontractors, with penalties for violations, but would not apply to sole-source contracts.

bill.title: Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-82.
subjects: War crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity

industries.rationale: The bill creates new procedural pathways and limits defenses in civil litigation, expanding the scope and duration of claims that law firms may pursue or defend.
Museums and cultural institutions that hold or exhibit artwork are directly affected by expanded liability and procedural rules for restitution claims.
Banks and auction houses that handle art transactions or hold art as collateral face potential claims if works in their possession are subject to restitution.

bill.plainSummary: This bill removes the 2026 deadline for filing lawsuits to recover art and other property taken during Nazi persecution between 1933 and 1945. It makes it easier to sue foreign governments and defendants located anywhere in the United States, and it blocks certain legal defenses that courts have used to dismiss these claims, such as arguments that too much time has passed. The changes apply to cases already filed as well as future ones.

bill.latestActionText: Message received in Senate: Returned to the Senate pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 212.

industries.rationale: The bill directly nullifies a reporting rule imposed on digital asset brokers and DeFi platforms, eliminating a new regulatory compliance obligation.
Traditional financial institutions that offer digital asset services would be relieved of the broker reporting requirements this rule imposed.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would block a December 2024 IRS rule that requires brokers and platforms facilitating digital asset (cryptocurrency) sales to report transaction details and gross proceeds to the IRS. The rule was designed to improve tax compliance by ensuring the IRS receives information about cryptocurrency sales, similar to reporting requirements for stocks and other securities. If passed, the resolution would nullify this reporting requirement before it takes effect.

bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-1.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-26.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

bill.title: Stop Russian Market Manipulation Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: The bill directly restricts imports of eight specific metals and minerals, affecting companies that source, process, or trade these materials.
Manufacturers that rely on platinum-group metals, nickel, copper, or zinc as inputs would face supply-chain changes and potentially higher costs.
Defense contractors use platinum-group metals and specialty alloys in aerospace and weapons systems, making supply sourcing relevant.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would ban the import of eight minerals—platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium, nickel, copper, zinc, and braggite—if they are produced in Russia or by Russian entities. The ban would also cover minerals obtained through swaps or other arrangements designed to evade the restriction. The prohibition would remain in effect until one year after the President certifies that Russia has ended hostilities against Ukraine, and would resume if Russia restarts hostilities within three years.

bill.title: ANTE Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: The bill directly targets manufacturers from nonmarket economies that relocate production to third countries to evade tariffs, potentially subjecting them to equivalent duties.
Retailers importing goods from third countries that are produced by covered entities would face potential new tariffs on those products.
Technology manufacturers and electronics producers frequently source from or operate facilities in multiple countries and could be subject to these anti-evasion measures.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow the U.S. Trade Representative to investigate whether companies owned or controlled by nonmarket economies like China are setting up operations in other countries to avoid tariffs. If the investigation finds such evasion, the Trade Representative could impose tariffs on those goods equivalent to the original tariffs. A covered entity includes any business in which at least 25% of ownership is held by entities from a nonmarket economy country.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 461.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research and development of drugs and therapies for ALS and neurodegenerative diseases, affecting pharmaceutical and biotech companies developing these treatments.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS AWARD IS TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO THE PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION.  THE RECIPIENT WILL IMPLEMENT GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) REDUCTION PROGRAMS, POLICIES, PROJECTS, AND MEASURES IDENTIFIED IN THE COMMONWEALTH'S PRIORITY CLIMATE ACTION PLAN (PCAP) DEVELOPED UNDER THEIR CLIMATE POLLUTION REDUCTION GRANTS (CPRG) PLANNING GRANT. ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED THROUGH THIS GRANT WILL BENEFIT ALL RESIDENTS AND VISITORS TO THE COMMONWEALTH OF PENNSYLVANIA THROUGH FOUR MAIN OBJECTIVES: IMPLEMENTATION OF AMBITIOUS MEASURES THAT WILL ACHIEVE SIGNIFICANT CUMULATIVE GHG REDUCTIONS BY 2030 AND BEYOND; PURSUIT OF MEASURES THAT WILL ACHIEVE SUBSTANTIAL COMMUNITY BENEFITS, PARTICULARLY IN LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES; COMPLEMENTING OTHER FUNDING SOURCES TO MAXIMIZE THESE GHG REDUCTIONS AND COMMUNITY BENEFITS; AND, PURSUIT OF INNOVATIVE POLICIES AND PROGRAMS THAT ARE REPLICABLE AND CAN BE 'SCALED UP' ACROSS MULTIPLE JURISDICTIONS. ACTIVITIES:PENNSYLVANIA WILL CONDUCT ITS OWN SUBAWARD COMPETITION TO RE-EQUIP ANY INDUSTRIAL OR MANUFACTURING FACILITY WITH EQUIPMENT DESIGNED TO REDUCE GHG EMISSIONS. SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OF THE SUBAWARDEES WILL INCLUDE: ELECTRIFICATION TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS LOW- OR ZERO-CARBON PROCESS HEAT SYSTEMS, ELECTRIC HEAT PUMPS, COMBINED HEAT AND POWER (CHP) SYSTEMS, THERMAL STORAGE, AND OTHER HEATING SYSTEMS BASED ON ELECTRICITY, CLEAN HYDROGEN, BIOMASS, OR WASTE HEAT RECOVERY; ENERGY EFFICIENCY TECHNOLOGIES THOSE THAT REDUCE DIRECT FUEL OR ELECTRICITY USE, UTILIZE INSULATION, SENSORS, OR CONTROLS OR DEPLOY SMART ENERGY MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS OR OTHER ADVANCED ENERGY EFFICIENCY TECHNOLOGIES; INDUSTRIAL PROCESS EMISSIONS AND WASTE REDUCTION TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS THOSE THAT REDUCE WASTE IN INDUSTRIAL APPLICATIONS, INCLUDING INDUSTRIAL HEAT PUMPS, CHP SYSTEMS, OR ADVANCED RECYCLING APPROACHES; FUEL SWITCHING TECHNOLOGIES THAT ENABLE THE TRANSITION TO LOW CARBON FUELS SUCH AS FLUIDIZED BED BIOMASS FURNACES, SOLAR-THERMAL HEATING SYSTEMS, AND DIRECT REDUCED IRON SHAFT FURNACES DESIGNED OR RETROFITTED FOR HYDROGEN-BASED REDUCTION; ON-SITE RENEWABLE ENERGY TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEMS, WIND TURBINES, MICRO-HYDROPOWER, OR GEOTHERMAL; CARBON CAPTURE, UTILIZATION, AND STORAGE (CCUS) TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS FLUE GAS CARBON CAPTURE SYSTEMS OR CALCIUM LOOPING CO2 CAPTURE SYSTEMS; FUGITIVE EMISSIONS REDUCTION TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS REGENERATIVE THERMAL OXIDIZERS AND VENTILATION AIR SYSTEMS; AND ANY OTHER TECHNOLOGY THAT REDUCES INDUSTRIAL GHG EMISSIONS, AS DETERMINED BY DEP. 
SUBRECIPIENT:SMALL-, MEDIUM- AND LARGE-SCALE GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS REDUCTION PROJECTS FOR INDUSTRIAL DECARBONZATION WILL BE COMPETITIVELY AWARDED EITHER DIRECTLY BY PADEP OR BY ITS SUBRECIPIENT PENNTAP. 
OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE: STANDING UP A STATEWIDE INDUSTRIAL DECARBONIZATION GRANT PROGRAM; COMPLETING 100-1,657 SMALL-SCALE PROJECTS, 5-50 MEDIUM-SCALE PROJECTS, AND 1-7 LARGE-SCALE PROJECTS; REDUCING AIR POLLUTANTS INCLUDING CAPS AND HAPS THROUGHOUT PENNSYLVANIA AND IN LOW INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES (LIDACS); SUBMISSION OF COMMUNITY BENEFITS PLANS (CBPS); AND PUBLISHING AN INDUSTRIAL DECARBONIZATION PLAYBOOK WITH CASE STUDIES DESCRIBING SUCCESSFUL PROJECTS. 

THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE: REDUCTION IN CUMULATIVE METRIC TONS OF GHG EMISSIONS, INCLUDING 4,332,303 METRIC TONS CO2E FROM 2025-2030 AND 8,047,294 METRIC TONS CO2E FROM 2025-2050; REDUCTION IN ANNUAL CRITERIA AIR POLLUTANTS, INCLUDING PARTICULATE MATTER (BOTH PM2.5 AND PM10), CARBON MONOXIDE, SULFUR DIOXIDE, OZONE, AND NITROGEN DIOXIDE, AND HAZARDOUS AIR POLLUTANTS, INCLUDING HYDROGEN SULFIDE, BENZENE, TOLUENE, ETHYLBENZENE,  XYLENE, HEXANE, ETHANE, PENTANE, FORMALDEHYDE, BUTANE, DICHLOROBENZENE, AND PROPANE, IN LIDACS IN 2030; LOWER ENERGY DEMAND AND INDUSTRIAL ENERGY EXPENDITURES; ENHANCED LEVEL OF COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT; CREATION OF HIGH-QUALITY JOBS; AND REDUCI

APPLICATION PURPOSE: TO PROVIDE FUNDS FOR THE CRITICAL REPLACEMENT OF THE MARKET-FRANKFORD LINE FLEET.; ACTIVITIES PERFORMED: MARKET FRANKFORD LINE FLEET REPLACEMENT; EXPECTED OUTCOMES: CONTINUE TO PROVIDE CLEAN SAFE AND RELIABLE TRANSPORTATION AND TO IMPROVE MOBILITY AND ACCESS THROUGHOUT THE PHILADELPHIA REGION.; INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: PROVIDE TRANSPORTATION SERVICES TO RESIDENTS/TRAVELERS IN THE PHILADELPHIA PA REGION.; SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: N/A
